transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-16 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega (Redwood); Priya Nair, Ethan Clarke, Rowena Park, Samir Patel (Voyager)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood runs through proposed extension with a 10% capacity uplift and EU/APAC activation. Discussion of failover verification, canary routing, and KMS integration. Customer requests runbook and security checklist. Next steps and owners assigned.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we've got about 45 minutes, this is Maya from Redwood, luis is with me. how are you all doing?
[00:06] Priya Nair: good, thanks, running behind on a few things but all good, appreciate the catch-up.
[00:12] Luis Ortega: cool, quick agenda — renewal term & contract extension ask, proposed capacity uplift, region activation checklist for eu/apac, and then the failover/canary validation that you asked about.
[00:22] Ethan Clarke: yeah mostly interested in the failover details, we saw a few tokenized timeouts last quarter and want to understand reroute behavior. also curious on the cost delta if we spin up eu nodes.
[00:35] Maya Chen: totally — high level, for the extension we're proposing a 12-month addendum to the current retainer with a 10% reserved capacity bump and optional burst credits. that lets you keep steady throughput and have room for spikes.
[00:50] Priya Nair: 10% is fine as a start, but can we define the SLA floor for p90 latency when traffic is routed to eu region? customers in EU need sub-120ms p90 for shorter prompts.
[01:05] Luis Ortega: yes — on our Dedicated/reserved tiers we target p90 under 120ms for short-turn gen on eu nodes; for larger context windows it'll be higher. I will share the per-model perf sheet later but rough numbers align with that SLO. transcriptions sometimes show model names weird, but we use optimized kernels per arch.
[01:23] Samir Patel: on failover - when primary region is overloaded what exactly happens? do we fail open to hosted variant or do we drop? last time a fallback sent to a different model and cost spiked.
[01:36] Maya Chen: good callout. The routing policy we recommended is layered: primary -> local region -> compatible variant in alternate region with graceful downgrade. so you can choose fallback model family (same size or smaller) and we can cap token budget to control cost. The automatic fallback can be configured to require explicit approval for model-family switch.
[01:57] Rowena Park: security wise, we need to know about KMS integration and key residency. if you're doing eu private, we need the HSM/KMS attestation and audit log retention details.
[02:08] Luis Ortega: for Private/VPC deployments we integrate with customer KMS; for hosted we'll show how to configure keywrap — attaching the KMS info and an attestation doc is on our deliverable list. There might be a small lag for key rotation events but audit logs are retained per the agreed retention window.
[02:24] Ethan Clarke: can you walk through the canary steps for a regional activation? we need to see how traffic shifts and how to measure regressions.
[02:33] Luis Ortega: sure — our recommended canary: 1) create a new route pointing to eu cluster, 2) send 1% of production traffic for 24 hours, 3) run prompt-regression suite against a curated set, 4) monitor latency, token cost, and quality deltas; if all pass, ramp to 10% for 12h then to 50% then full. we'll provide the runbook with concrete curl/SDK examples.
[02:57] Priya Nair: that 24-hour window — can you be explicit about what metrics you'll provide and where? we need token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, error traces and an eval score for our prompt families.
[03:12] Maya Chen: absolutely — Console exports token breakdown, per-route latency hist, trace ids, and quality regression scores if you feed in the evaluation prompt set. we'll include the dashboard links in the playbook.
[03:25] Samir Patel: earlier you mentioned KV cache — last time the cache warmed slowly in a different region and that caused cold-start latencies. is there a prefix caching strategy for multi-region?
[03:34] Luis Ortega: yes, we do prefix/KV caching and have a warming plan; for region bring-up we can pre-warm hot keys and pin important session KV into the eu cluster. there are edge cases around cold start for big context windows but warming helps.
[03:52] Ethan Clarke: cost — what's the delta per token in eu vs current region? we run about 1.2B tokens/month.
[03:59] Maya Chen: short answer: eu dedicated nodes have a modest uplift (roughly +12% per-token at list) due to infra costs, but with prefix caching and batching suggestions we usually see net cost impact lower — maybe +5% effective after optimization. we'll send the cost appendix showing per-model delta.
[04:20] Priya Nair: ok good. On contract — we want to extend for 12 months but would like a 60-day exit window in case production regressions are observed after activation. can you accommodate that?
[04:34] Maya Chen: we can offer a limited exit clause tied to measurable quality regressions in the first 30-60 days post-activation. the clause needs to be scoped to regressions on agreed eval sets and thresholds; legal will draft the exact language.
[04:50] Rowena Park: also need SOC2 artifacts and any penetration test records you can share that are redacted. plus a KMS attestation.
[04:59] Luis Ortega: noted — we'll include SOC2 self-attestation and the summary of our pen test; full reports require an NDA but we can share the summary and control mappings. KMS attestation doc will be included.
[05:12] Samir Patel: about failover tests — can Redwood run simulated outage and we can monitor from our side? we're thinking a 2-hour window where you force routing to eu/pinned variant.
[05:21] Maya Chen: yes we can coordinate a scheduled failover window; we'll provide the runbook and rollback steps. For safety we'll keep throttles and token caps at each step so risk is minimal.
[05:33] Ethan Clarke: what about throttling policies — can we enforce per-customer caps to protect downstream services?
[05:38] Luis Ortega: we have route-level throttles, token caps, and quota buckets. you can set per-route SLOs and hard caps to prevent cost runaway.
[05:46] Priya Nair: one operational ask — we need developer-level access patterns. Our devs want a staging route that mirrors prod but with quota limits. can that be done quickly?
[05:55] Maya Chen: yes, staging routes are easy — we'll create a staging model route mapped to a smaller cluster, share API keys (scoped with RBAC), and you can test without touching prod.
[06:08] Rowena Park: about data residency — for EU nodes, are logs and KV retained in-region by default? we need assurance for GDPR.
[06:16] Luis Ortega: for private/eu-hosted variants you can elect in-region retention; for hosted global accounts we can set retention to eu by customer and mask egress. We'll put the exact config steps in the security appendix.
[06:29] Maya Chen: quick recap — Redwood to produce: cost appendix, canary runbook, security appendix (SOC2 summary + KMS attestation), and propose failover test windows. Voyager to send prompt families and VPC details.
[06:45] Priya Nair: sounds right. timelines? we need the docs before our 10/28 ops blackout where we plan the activation.
[06:53] Maya Chen: we'll target 10/20 for docs and propose failover on 10/28 — if that works on your side we'll lock it in.
[07:01] Ethan Clarke: couple of micro-questions — latency to eu from our frankfurt infra, and is there an ops contact in the event of anomalies?
[07:08] Luis Ortega: frankfurt to our eu cluster should be ~25-45ms depending on path; we'll provide traceroutes during validation. Ops contact — you'll get a named oncall for that window plus escalation steps listed.
[07:20] Samir Patel: curious — any recommended quan-tization changes for cost reduction? last time some of our smaller models saw a quality dip.
[07:28] Luis Ortega: we recommend model-specific quant profiles; for some families 4-bit q8xx offered good savings with minimal quality loss, but we'll run a small eval on your prompt set. that's part of the optimization suggestions.
[07:43] Maya Chen: ok any other blockers?
[07:46] Rowena Park: just one — egress IPs need to be static for our firewall rules. you said you could provide a range?
[07:54] Luis Ortega: yes we'll provide the list of egress IPs for the eu cluster; for private deployments you'll be able to pin.
[08:02] Priya Nair: great. final ask — can you include an example SLA credit calculation for a missed p95 target? legal wants to see the math.
[08:11] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include an SLA example table in the appendix, and legal can iterate.
[08:18] [wrap up]
[08:20] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll send the docs and follow up with the proposed failover window.
[08:24] Priya Nair: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:26] Ethan Clarke: thanks all.

End of transcript.
